Q: How to hide root-level files using git sparse-checkout in cone mode? A:

You need to respect the tradeoff cone mode makes: quick response in large checkouts in exchange for losing some precision, precision that can get slow to calculate as checkout trees grow.

If you don't have a notably large checkout, you can set your sparsity rules up as --no-cone and stay happy as long as the cost remains negligible.

Q: git stash failed when trying to perform a git pull A:

The error fatal: stash failed indicates that an operation akin to git stash was attempted.

There is a configuration option pull.autoStash. It looks like this is enabled in this repository.

If that is the case, you can temporarily disable the option with

git pull --no-autostash origin master

This may still fail, but this time because there are uncommitted modifications in the worktree. The real solution is then, of course, to handle the uncommitted changes, i.e., either to commit them or to discard them.

Q: How to fix ClientError: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the CreateBucket operation: Access Denied when calling create_bucket A:

I encountered the same issue while running on EC2 instance and its seems that for using credentials for Amazon EC2 you need to follow these instructions https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-metadata.html

Q: How to write the xxd command in cmd in windows A:

Late to the party to add, enhancing luk-aron answer, that if you have git for Windows the actual program is likely stored as C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\xxd.exe, so you can call it how you like by using the full name, or adding the directory path to your PATH environment variable, or (if you have MSYS2 bash) with an alias/symlink. I chose the second and now simply calling xxd works in bash.
